task: set up a new device through its companion app or on-device flow: a new phone (setup, account sign-in, data transfer), a router or mesh Wi-Fi via its app, a smartwatch pairing, or a smart-home device (camera, plug, speaker, doorbell): the unbox-to-working arc — pair or connect, sign in, configure the essentials; complete when the device shows working/connected in the app or the phone reaches its fully set-up home screen. Surface pinned: the setup flow itself — not unboxing-only or review videos.

tree.label: Set up a new device
tree.note: do 1, then 2. phone routes then do 3 and 4, where 4.3 is the whole of 4. accessory routes do 4 first, then 2.5 to 2.8, then 3 - the app will not look for a device until it knows the account. then 5 where anything is carried over; uSN0 and DT4C's first pass skip it outright. then 6. 7 always, and 7.9 when 7 comes back wrong. 8 on the transfer routes, reaching into 1.10 where the erase is actually run (aawv). 9 where the device has services to configure - fok5 and NZzD do parts of it inside 6, u--l does all of it after 7.

children.label: Prepare the devices
children.note: 1.1 to 1.3 on boxed hardware only (NZzD, u--l, fok5, 9yTg); 1.4 when the hardware will not enter setup mode (9yTg). 1.5 and 1.6 on the devices being replaced, in any order. 1.7 first on the new device, and 1.10 when the answer is wrong (mIjR, _CVz). 1.8 where a transfer will run long (aawv, CKwc). 1.9 where the route leans on a backup - CKwc and _CVz satisfy it by reading a timestamp instead of running one. 1.10 also serves goal 8: the same erase, at the other end of the task.
